constraints.source_text: If a student uses a course to satisfy a requirement or elective that has already been taken in the track requirements, it can not be double-counted as the cross-cutting course. The cross-cutting course must be a different course.
constraints.description: A course already used to satisfy track requirements cannot be double-counted as the cross-cutting topics course.

details.scope: track requirements and cross-cutting topics course

constraints.source_text: All students will take 4 units of a capstone experience during their senior year. This may be fulfilled by taking PPD 431 Undergraduate Policy, Planning, and Development Studio (4) or PPD 497a Senior Thesis , PPD 497b Senior Thesis (2-2).
constraints.description: Students must complete a 4-unit capstone experience, choosing between PPD 431 or the PPD 497a/497b sequence.

constraints.source_text: Students wishing to enroll in PPD 497a , PPD 497b must have a 3.7 GPA in PPD courses and an overall 3.5 GPA.
constraints.description: Enrollment in the PPD 497a/PPD 497b capstone alternative requires meeting specific GPA thresholds.
constraints.note: Treated as an entry gate for an alternate capstone option rather than a plain GPA floor.

constraints.source_text: Public Policy majors are required to complete 140 hours of internship by enrolling in PPD 301 PPD Practices: Internship Seminar or the Washington, D.C., Semester internship.
constraints.description: Students must complete 140 hours of internship via PPD 301 or the D.C. Semester internship.

details.setting: internship (PPD 301 or Washington, D.C., Semester internship)

unclassified.source_text: A minimum grade of C, 2.0 (A = 4.0), must be earned in each of the pre-major courses.
unclassified.why: This is a minimum-grade requirement, which the taxonomy explicitly drops as out of scope.

unclassified.source_text: All pre-major requirements must be taken for a letter grade.
unclassified.why: This is a grading-mode requirement (letter grade vs. pass/no-pass), out of scope per taxonomy.

unclassified.source_text: Students may work with their adviser for approval to take track electives outside of the courses listed to meet their academic needs.
unclassified.why: This is a discretionary substitution allowance without a defined pool or specific action, more advisory/procedural than a concrete constraint to encode.

unclassified.source_text: Graduate courses in the subject area may be selected in consultation and with the approval of the adviser.
unclassified.why: Advisory/discretionary allowance rather than a binding requirement with a defined pool.

unclassified.source_text: For the two track requirements that consist of a choice (POSC 340 or LAW 300 and LAW 200w or PPD 357 ), the courses not used to satisfy these requirements may be taken as electives.
unclassified.why: This describes an optional allowance about elective reuse rather than a binding requirement.

unclassified.source_text: If not used to satisfy the core track requirement, either PPD 427L or DSCI 250 may be selected as an elective.
unclassified.why: Optional allowance describing possible reuse, not a binding requirement itself.

unclassified.source_text: Other elective courses may be selected in consultation with the adviser.
unclassified.why: Advisory/discretionary statement without a defined pool or firm requirement.

unclassified.source_text: Price School honors are available at graduation to qualified PPD majors and result in a special designation of departmental honors on a student’s transcript. Achievement of PPD honors requires a 3.7 GPA in PPD major courses and a 3.5 overall GPA as well as nomination by the professor in the capstone experience. In addition, students must earn an A in their capstone course (PPD 497a , PPD 497b or PPD 431 ).
unclassified.why: Optional honors track, explicitly out of scope per taxonomy.

unclassified.source_text: It is taken preferably junior year after completion of the core curriculum.
unclassified.why: Advisory timing preference ('preferably'), not a binding sequencing rule.
